commonErrors.why: You multiply the force by the mass. The relationship is F = ma, so the acceleration is F/m not F × m; And your output unit is N·kg which is not acceleration.
You divide the mass by the force. Review which two quantities are in the numerator.
You wrote the mass. Weight is a force whose unit is a newton, and mass is a quantity of matter whose unit is a kilogram. They are two different quantities, not measures of the same thing.
You divided the mass by g instead of multiplying it by it.
You used g = 10 even though the question specified 9.8. Approximation is acceptable when left up to you, not when the value is given.
You calculated mg and neglected the acceleration. The equality N = mg requires that there be no vertical acceleration, which is a condition that is violated here.
You counted ma alone. This is the resultant force, not the ground force; Floor force includes balancing weight as well.

You subtracted the acceleration instead of adding it, and calculated m(g − a). This works for an elevator accelerating downward; Here the acceleration is upward, so the force is greater than the weight, not smaller.

questions.solution: The resultant 15 − 9.0 = 6.0 N to the right, then a = 6.0/2.0 = 3.0 m/s².

commonErrors.why: You added the two forces instead of subtracting them. Forces are vectors, and opposites are subtracted. If they were combined, the acceleration would be greater, even though one hinders the other.
You stopped at the net force and did not divide it by the mass. Your output unit is N and the question is for m/s².
You divided by the power or multiplied by the mass instead of dividing by it.

questions.solution: By Newton's third law, the two forces are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction: 10 N. It does not depend on mass or acceleration. However, the box accelerates because the force of your hand affects it, and its force affects you.

commonErrors.why: You multiply the force by the mass. The reaction is always equal to the action, It has nothing to do with the mass of either body.
You divided the force by the mass and calculated the acceleration 2.5 m/s², not the force. Pay attention to the desired unit.
You thought that the reaction cancels out the action, so the result is zero. The two forces are on two different bodies, so they do not come together in one diagram or cancel out.
